key_insight: Centering impacted stakeholders in automatic speech recognition (ASR) audits reveals real-world performance gaps, contextual harms, and governance priorities that conventional technical benchmarks miss, enabling more actionable and socially responsive evaluations.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap between technical ASR evaluation and real-world harms by creating an audit approach that integrates the perspectives, needs, and priorities of people most affected by ASR failures (e.g., dialect speakers, marginalized groups, service users).
method: Stakeholder-driven audit design: co‑design audit goals, metrics, and threat models with impacted communities, practitioners, and regulators.
Mixed-method evaluation: combine quantitative performance metrics (error rates by language/dialect, demographic slices) with qualitative evidence (user interviews, contextual harm case studies).
Iterative governance loop: perform audits, surface prioritized harms, document limitations, and feed findings back into model development, deployment controls, and public reporting.
impact: Provides AI/ML teams a practical framework to detect and mitigate ASR disparities, improve deployment decisions, and strengthen accountability and trust by aligning evaluation with societal impacts rather than solely aggregate benchmarks.
visual_elements: Process diagram: stakeholder-in-the-loop audit lifecycle (co‑design → testing → analysis → remediation → reporting).
Bar/heatmap chart: ASR error rates broken down by language, dialect, and demographic groups to show disparities.
Mixed-methods panel: paired qualitative quotes or vignettes beside quantitative metrics illustrating contextual harms.
Checklist/scorecard icon: audit deliverables (metrics, documentation, mitigation action plan, public summary).
paper_title: The case for stakeholder-driven AI auditing in automatic speech recognition
paper_authors: Mona Sloane, Hilke Schellmann, Katelyn Xiaoying Mei, Anna Seo Gyeong Choi, Allison Koenecke
